title: DRE schedules
description: The schedules file, `schedules.yml`: a list of named schedules.

schedule.description: One named schedule. DRE doesn't fire it; your orchestrator runs `dre run --schedule <name>`.

name.description: The schedule's name: letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit. Unique across the project.

report.description: The report to run. Use `report` or `select`, not both.

set.description: The Set of `report` to run. Only with `report`.

select.description: A selector for the reports to run, e.g. `tag:regulatory`. Use `report` or `select`, not both.

vars.description: Variables for the run: above the report's own and below `--var`.

timing.description: The name of a timing in `timings.yml` to fire on. Use `timing` or one of `cron`, `every`, `rrule`; with `timing`, the schedule sets none of the timing's keys (`timezone`, `starting`, `at`, `except`, `also`).

timezone.description: The timezone it fires in, and the one `run.date` and `run.now` use, an IANA name such as `Australia/Sydney`. Default: the project's `timezone:` for firing (the report's for the run), then UTC.

enabled.description: `false` pauses the schedule: it keeps its name and settings but `dre schedule ls` lists no occurrences for it. Default: `true`.

cron.description: A cron expression (5 fields, or a macro such as `@daily`). A schedule needs exactly one of `timing`, `cron`, `every` or `rrule`.

every.description: Every N days, weeks or months, with exactly one unit, e.g. `{days: 3}`.

rrule.description: An iCalendar recurrence rule, e.g. `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=2TU`. Use `starting` for a rule with `INTERVAL` above 1 or `COUNT`, and `at` for its time of day.

starting.description: With `every` or `rrule`: the first date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. `every` needs it, and so does a rule with `INTERVAL` above 1, a `COUNT`, or a day it takes from its start.

at.description: With `every` or `rrule`: the time of day, `HH:MM` (24-hour), unless the rule sets `BYHOUR`/`BYMINUTE`. Default: 00:00.

except.description: Dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`, in its timezone) it doesn't fire on, e.g. holidays.

also.description: Extra dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`) it fires on, at its time of day in its timezone. Needs a timing that fires at one time of day.
